summary: New identity_resolution.py: handle-shaped (email or registry) recall queries resolve by exact reverse lookup instead of similarity search. Detection is conservative (exactly one email-shaped token, or the whole query with interrogative framing stripped exactly matching a registry.json handle value); a non-handle query falls through byte-identically (proven against _recall_via_backend directly). Resolution walk mirrors corrections._resolve_email_handle (email via pii.ExcludedRecordIndex.all_by_identifier, registry via corrections.load_registry + _handle_matches); closed reason vocabulary no-match/record-without-uid/ambiguous/orphan-uid. with_pii gating reuses the athenaeum#885 layer ordering exactly (audience filter, then athenaeum#532 recallable drop, both before any excluded-surface lookup, zero-scan proof for both drops using a registry handle); response shape follows the EntityRead/RedactionMarker precedent (with_pii=True populates contact_values with per-value usage/provenance classification + bounce + validity facts, with_pii=False populates field-level redaction markers instead). No outreach_eligible or any action predicate anywhere in the output -- ContactValueFact is built field-by-field. Wired into both recall_search (MCP) and cmd_recall (CLI), each making one call into the shared resolver. Docs note in docs/recall-architecture.md, CHANGELOG updated. Gates green: ruff check + ruff format clean on new files, mypy clean, full pytest suite 4845 passed / 113 skipped / 40 deselected / 1 xfailed, 32 pre-existing failures (git-subprocess/sandbox-environment issues) verified identical against a clean develop checkout via git stash compare -- zero failures introduced. 100% line coverage of the new module.
